questions.stem: Two spherical raindrops of equal size fall through air with terminal velocity of $10\ \mathrm{cm/s}$. If they coalesce to form a single drop, its terminal velocity will be:
questions.solution:
Terminal velocity $v_t \propto r^2$.
When two drops of radius $r$ coalesce, the volume is doubled:
$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 2 \left(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right) \implies R = 2^{1/3} r$.
Since $v_t \propto r^2$, the new terminal velocity is $v_t' = v_t \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2 = 10 \times (2^{1/3})^2 = 10 \times 2^{2/3}\ \mathrm{cm/s}$.

questions.stem: Eight identical spherical raindrops falling down with terminal velocity $v$ merge to form a single large drop. The terminal velocity of the new large drop is:
questions.solution:
Volume remains conserved: $8 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \implies R = 2r$.
Terminal velocity $v_T \propto r^2$. Therefore, $v' = v \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2 = v(2)^2 = 4v$.

questions.stem: A small spherical ball of radius $r$ falls from rest in a viscous liquid. Due to friction, heat is produced. The rate of production of heat when the ball attains terminal velocity is proportional to:
questions.solution:
Rate of heat production (power) is $P = F_v \cdot v_t = (6\pi\eta r v_t) v_t = 6\pi\eta r v_t^2$.
Since terminal velocity $v_t \propto r^2$,
$P \propto r \cdot (r^2)^2 = r^5$.

questions.stem: Two spherical rain drops of equal size falling through air have steady terminal velocity of $1\ \mathrm{cm/s}$. If the two drops coalesce to form a single larger drop, the terminal velocity of the new drop is:
questions.solution:
Terminal velocity $v_t \propto r^2$.
When two drops coalesce, the volume is conserved:
$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 2 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \implies R = 2^{1/3} r$.
Therefore, $v_t' \propto R^2 \implies v_t' = v_t \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2 = 1 \times (2^{1/3})^2 = 2^{2/3}\ \mathrm{cm/s}$.
